label: input token l at a late original position (t >= 5)
explanation: Fires only on the input token l during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, and only at positions t >= 5. It fires on every such step (recall 1.0). At t = 5 it fires on about 18% of them and only weakly (2.7% of activation mass). From t >= 6 it fires on all of them (precision 1.0 for t >= 6) and accounts for 97% of the mass. Magnitude grows with position: the strongest activations (about 3.0) come when l is the last original token right before <DEL> (to_go = 0) in long sequences. It never fires on other tokens, on l at t <= 4, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase, including when l is being output or fed back in. It does not depend on the previous tokens or the first token.

issues: Factual error in the explanation: it says the feature fires on about 18% of l inputs at t = 5. Scoring (phase==0)&(in_tok==l)&(t==5) gives precision 0.527 on test, so it fires on about 53% of them. The 18% figure is wrong (it may be confused with t=5's share of active steps, which is 26% on test). The 2.7% mass figure is right (test mass recall 0.026), and these activations sit only in the lowest activation quartile.

All 5247 test false positives of the original predicate are l inputs at step 5. This is one weak, near-threshold class, not scattered noise. It is the only gap: there are 0 missed activations, and t >= 6 has precision 1.0.

The claim 'no dependence on previous tokens' is slightly off at t = 5. When the previous token is a digit, the feature fires on 77% of l inputs at t=5, versus 50% otherwise. No clean history rule separates the t=5 cases: seen(l), first_tok, n_digits and vowels each move the rate by 5 points or less. So the t=5 behaviour looks like a graded, near-threshold activation, not a distinct rule.

Other claims check out. The feature never fires in the delimiter or copy phase (0 active of about 3.2M steps), never on any token other than l, and never at t <= 4. Activation mass rises with L and is highest when to_go = 0: L=9 carries 55% of the mass and to_go=0 carries 55%.

Alternatives are not better. Tightening to t >= 6 gives test F1 0.851 (precision 1.0, recall 0.74, mass recall 0.974). Adding L >= 7 gives F1 0.887. Both are worse than the original 0.896, so the original predicate remains the best simple rule.
skeptic.revised_label: input token l at original position t >= 6 (and weakly, about half the time, at t = 5); strength grows with position and with L

final_label: input token l at original position t >= 6 (and weakly, about half the time, at t = 5); strength grows with position and with L
